catchment: Catchment Areas: Alwar, Bharatpur, Dausa, Jaipur, Nagaur (Rajasthan); Agra, Mathura, Hathras, Budaun (Uttar Pradesh); Mahendragarh, Rewari, Bhiwani (Haryana).

paragraphs.text: 1. Northwestern Commercial Food & Milling Corridor (Rajasthan, UP & Haryana)
Strategic Role: India's primary aggregation and processing belt for food-grade Kharif pearl millet, supplying the urban consumption markets of Delhi-NCR, Northern India, and Central India.

Key Facilities: Large automated grain cleaning and optical Sortex grading units in Alwar, Chomu (Jaipur), Agra, and Aligarh; stabilization and flour-milling units supplying consumer brands (Aashirvaad, Tata Soulfull).
Catchment Areas: Alwar, Bharatpur, Dausa, Jaipur, Nagaur (Rajasthan); Agra, Mathura, Hathras, Budaun (Uttar Pradesh); Mahendragarh, Rewari, Bhiwani (Haryana).

summary.text: In Indian agricultural economics (Directorate of Economics and Statistics / Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare / ICAR-IIMR), Bajra (Pennisetum glaucum, Pearl Millet) is the most widely cultivated Shree Anna (Nutri-Cereal) in India. India is the largest producer of pearl millet globally, accounting for roughly 40% to 45% of total world production.

cells: HHB-67 Improved, RHB-177, RHB-223, MPMH-17, Proagro 9444, Pioneer 86M84
National "Bajra Bowl" & Heartland; largest global acreage; essential food and dry fodder (Karbi) staple

Highest State Productivity (>2,200–2,500 kg/ha); mechanized hybrid bajra; MSP procurement

Chambal/Gwalior ravines and plains; supplies northern industrial and feed mandis

Rain-shadow Western Ghats & Marathwada; pioneer of high-iron biofortification

Northern dry zone (Sajje); intercropped in red and light black soils
CO-9, CO-10, CO(Cu)-9, TNAU Cumbu Hybrid CO-9
Year-round rainfed/irrigated red loams (Kambu); porridge & poultry feed
Semi-arid Rayalaseema and South Telangana drylands
Peri-urban dairy green fodder tracts and summer forage

protection.name: Downy Mildew / "Green Ear Disease" (Sclerospora graminicola)
protection.geography: All-India Commercial Belts (Heavy in Rajasthan, Haryana, Gujarat)
protection.impact: Systemic infection causing chlorosis on leaves; leaves turn white/yellow with downy white fungal growth underneath; infected earheads transform into a twisted, bushy mass of tiny, green, leaf-like structures ("Green Ear"), completely suppressing seed formation; causes 20–50% yield losses.
protection.passage: Bajra — source table 102, row 2. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Ergot / "Sugary Disease" (Claviceps fusiformis)
protection.geography: Humid Flowering Periods (Rain-hit Kharif tracts across all states)
protection.impact: Sticky, pinkish-to-amber honey-like droplets (honeydew) ooze from infected spikelets during flowering; droplets harden into dark brown or black, elongated sclerotial bodies (ergot kernels); contains toxic alkaloids (agroclavine); grains with  ergot are poisonous to livestock and humans.
protection.passage: Bajra — source table 102, row 3. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Smut (Moesziomyces penicillariae)
protection.geography: All Sandy & Arid Belts (Severe in Rajasthan, Haryana, MP)
protection.impact: Individual ovaries in the earhead swell into large, greenish-to-dark brown sacks (sori), bulging between the glumes; sori rupture at maturity, releasing millions of dark brown, airborne teliospores; ruins seed viability and grain color.
protection.passage: Bajra — source table 102, row 4. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Rust (Puccinia substriata)
protection.geography: Post-Monsoon & Late Kharif Belts (Heavy in Gujarat, Maharashtra, TN)
protection.impact: Minute, reddish-orange to dark brown pustules appear on both upper and lower leaf surfaces; pustules coalesce, causing premature leaf drying and senescence; suppresses grain filling and degrades forage fodder quality.
protection.passage: Bajra — source table 102, row 5. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Shoot Fly (Atherigona soccata) & Stem Borer (Chilo partellus)
protection.geography: Early Vegetative & Seedling Stage (All Commercial Belts)
protection.impact: Shoot fly maggots cut the central seedling shoot, forming dead hearts; stem borer caterpillars feed in the leaf whorl (pinholes) and tunnel inside the main culm, causing stem breakage and chaffy spikes.
protection.passage: Bajra — source table 102, row 6. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Rice Weevil & Rust-Red Flour Beetle (Sitophilus oryzae, Tribolium castaneum)
protection.impact: Adult beetles and larvae bore into stored whole bajra kernels; hollow out grains, generating powdery flour frass and causing rapid lipid oxidation and foul odors; degrades seed quality.
protection.passage: Bajra — source table 102, row 7. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.
